added.S3-N2: The dashboard shows no "Last updated" line or any other freshness indicator. Its figures are never behind the reports (S3-R1), so there is nothing to be out of date.
added.S4-R11b: The sparkline shows direction, not level. Each tile scales its line between its own lowest and highest point, so a figure that never changes over the range (for example Technician Utilization at 100% on every day) draws as a flat line along the bottom of the trend area, whatever the figure is. The headline carries the actual value. The start-at-0 axis of S9-R8 applies to the expanded and report charts, which have an axis, not to the sparkline.
added.S5-N3: The inactivity window has one control, the pill on the At Risk Customers tile. The expanded At Risk Customers table follows it (S5-R12) and has no inactivity control of its own.
added.S6-R3a: The expanded Revenue chart covers the tile's own date range (S7-R5), with one bar per day, week, month or quarter chosen from the length of the range by the same rule as the sparkline (S4-R11). Last 12 Months shows twelve monthly bars; This Month shows daily bars.
added.S6-R8a: In the At Risk Customers table, a customer's twelve-month revenue is a link that opens the Sales report filtered to that customer over the same twelve months the amount covers, so the report total equals the amount. A walk-in row, or an amount of $0.00, is plain text.
added.S7-R2a: The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a **Today** button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).
added.S9-R10: Hovering a name in a chart legend shows that person's most recent value and the month it is from, for example "120% · Aug 2026". It shows no average; the table beside the chart gives the figure for the whole range.
added.S9-R11: An expanded chart with nothing to show for the selected range reads "No data for selected date range", the message these charts already use in production. The dashed empty-chart outline is only for the sparkline on a tile (S4-R12 to S4-R18).
added.S9-R9: In an expanded chart, a month with no value is drawn as a dashed line joining the points on either side of it. This is how these charts already draw in production. A gap in the line applies only to the sparkline on a tile (S4-R11).
added.S11-E2: A chart on a report page with nothing to show for the selected range reads "No data for selected date range", the message these charts already use in production. It does not use the tile's dashed empty-chart outline.
added.S12-R10: A chart filter list that opens upward stays below the top menu bar and never covers it, for example by being shorter and scrolling inside (SV-11242).
added.S12-R11: In the dark theme, the whole tile date picker is dark, with near-white presets, range text and buttons, matching the report date filters (SV-11245).
added.S12-R12: On a small screen, every tile's date button opens its picker however far the page is scrolled (SV-11246).
added.S12-R13: On a small screen the page never scrolls sideways, whatever date range a tile shows. A long date label fits within its tile (SV-11255).
added.S12-R6: A report opened from a tile opens its Date filter panel once, in its final position, with no jump; the same as when the report is opened from the Reports menu (SV-10891).
added.S12-R7: On a 1536 × 864 screen at 100% zoom, a report showing its chart still shows table rows under the chart and lets the user scroll through them, without zooming out or hiding the chart (SV-10933).
added.S12-R8: With the chart showing, scrolling the table under it moves only the table rows; the chart and filters stay in place (SV-10934).
added.S12-R9: An open date picker on a tile never floats away from its tile. Scrolling with the pointer over the picker does not scroll the page (SV-10936).

S5-R9.old: The At Risk Customers tile shows a supporting line reading "${revenue} (12mo) · {count} customers" when more than one customer is at risk.
S5-R9.new: The At Risk Customers tile shows a supporting line reading "${revenue} (12mo) · {count} customers" when no customer or more than one customer is at risk. With none at risk it reads "$0.00 (12mo) · 0 customers", so the line never disappears.

non_code_diff: -The dashboard is read-only. It shows no toasts, alerts, or validation messages. The only user-facing feedback is a visual state: when every technician is deselected on a technician chart, that chart is hidden until at least one technician is selected again (S8-N1).
